meta.title: UK disability issues evidence
meta.note: Measures retain their original geography, period, population and definition. Comparisons do not imply causation.

items.title: Disabled employment rate
items.detail: 5.5 million disabled people were in employment. The employment gap was 29.7 percentage points.
items.caveat: Working-age people aged 16 to 64. The latest year-on-year change in the rate was not statistically significant.

items.title: Disability employment gap
items.detail: Difference between the employment rates of disabled and non-disabled people.
items.caveat: A gap describes a difference; it does not by itself identify the cause.

items.title: Relative low income after housing costs
items.detail: Share of individuals living in families where someone is disabled who were in relative low income after housing costs.
items.caveat: Family disability status and household income are associated in the data; several factors may contribute to the difference.

items.title: Relative low income before housing costs
items.comparison: 2 pp higher than families without a disabled member
items.detail: Relative low income before housing costs among individuals in families where someone is disabled.
items.caveat: The publication warns that disability-question changes can affect comparisons over time.

items.title: PIP claims with entitlement
items.detail: Claims with entitlement to Personal Independence Payment.
items.caveat: PIP caseload is not a count of all disabled people and does not cover Scotland's Adult Disability Payment caseload.

items.title: Universal Credit health caseload
items.detail: People on Universal Credit health, covering claimants with a health condition or disability restricting ability to work.
items.caveat: This is a benefits-system measure, not a measure of healthcare access or the total disabled population.

items.title: Trips made by disabled adults
items.detail: Average trips per person in 2025; disabled adults made 21% fewer trips.
items.caveat: Travel frequency does not on its own explain why trips differ. The survey excludes people living in care homes and some communal settings.

items.title: Pupils with an EHC plan
items.detail: Pupils in schools in England with an education, health and care plan.
items.caveat: EHC plans and SEN are not the same as disability status.

items.title: Pupils with SEN support
items.detail: Pupils receiving SEN support in England.
items.caveat: SEN is a school support classification and should not be treated as a direct count of disabled pupils.

items.title: Police-recorded disability hate crime
items.detail: Disability hate crime offences recorded by police.
items.caveat: Police-recorded offences do not measure all incidents; reporting and recording practices affect the count.

items.title: Civic engagement
items.detail: Disabled adults who took part in civic participation, consultation or activism at least once in the previous 12 months.
items.caveat: Disability status is self-reported. This is a participation measure, not a measure of accessibility or discrimination.

items.title: Social housing
items.detail: Working-age disabled people renting social housing.
items.caveat: This evidence is older than most other figures on the site and should not be presented as a current 2026 estimate.

items.title: Own home
items.detail: Working-age disabled people who owned their home.
items.caveat: This is older Annual Population Survey evidence for people aged 16 to 64.

items.title: Disability and deprivation at age 40–44
items.detail: Disabled 40- to 44-year-olds in the most deprived areas of England compared with the least deprived areas.
items.caveat: The figures show an association between deprivation and disability prevalence, not proof that one causes the other.

items.title: Census disability prevalence
items.detail: People classified as disabled under the Census 2021 question and definition.
items.caveat: Census 2021 uses a different source and age structure from the Family Resources Survey, so figures should not be treated as directly interchangeable.

items.title: Health & care evidence
items.comparison: No benefits data reused as healthcare data
items.detail: This release deliberately does not use Universal Credit Health or PIP as a proxy for healthcare access.
items.caveat: A future health section should use direct health-service, outcome or care datasets with clearly matched populations and definitions.
